question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x+7),$ the remainder equals $q(-7).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $2,$ then we must have $q(-7)=2.$

Evaluating $q(-7)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}q(-7) & =(-7)^{3}+7(-7)^{2}+(-7)+a \\  & =-343+343-7+a \\  & =-7+a,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that

$$
2=-7+a.
$$

Solving for $a$ in the equation above, we find that $a=9.$
